verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents some event-triggered automation of its own. Resource monitors let users set a credit-limit rule that automatically suspends a warehouse, and Snowpipe automatically loads files as they arrive in a stage. Streams only record changes "so that actions can be taken," which is a building block rather than a rule engine. The evidence shows narrow, fixed-purpose triggers, not general user-defined event rules. missing for 10: a general-purpose rule/trigger engine for arbitrary events and actions (e.g., documented alerts or tasks triggered by data conditions), evidence of AI-native rule definition, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can also set up a resource monitor to suspend a standard virtual warehouse or disable an Adaptive Warehouse when it reaches a credit limit.
Snowpipe continuously loads data from files into standard tables and Apache Iceberg™ tables as the files arrive in a stage.
